reasoning: A hybrid approach combines autonomous reasoning to identify obvious shared features across instances with external XAI tools to quantify feature importance and detect spurious correlations, ensuring both pattern recognition and statistical validation of feature influence. This strengthens confidence in identifying features that are present in all misclassified instances and have high model attribution despite being semantically unrelated to the target class.

autonomous_tasks.query: Which features are common across all three misclassified instances (13590, 2021, 12840)?
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A list of shared categorical and numerical features across all three instances

autonomous_tasks.query: Why might a shared feature—despite being semantically unrelated to income—have high predictive power in this model?
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A hypothesis about a potential spurious correlation involving the shared feature and the model's prediction

tool_selection.reasoning: SHAP provides a robust, game-theoretic attribution that identifies high-impact features across instances, especially useful to detect spurious features with high scores despite lack of semantic relevance. LIME and Integrated Gradients offer local and global interpretability to validate feature importance. Sensitivity analysis helps isolate how feature removal affects predictions, confirming whether a shared feature drives misclassification. Together, these tools validate both the presence and impact of spurious features in the model.
